root_motivation: host.trigger.set has no update verb: re-running it (an agent retargeting a hook, or a scheduled agent re-running its own setup script) always inserts, so the natural 'set it again' mints a duplicate trigger, eats a quota slot, and fires twice. The 2026-09-30 fleet board dogfood incident is the concrete case: retargeting a webhook minted a second trigger and consumed a free-plan webhook slot the coder had to remove by hand. This PRD gives every trigger a tenant-unique name (default <kind>:<tool_name>) and makes host.trigger.set an upsert keyed by that name: an existing same-kind trigger is updated in place (same id, same hook URL), a different-kind collision is refused, and every other trigger verb accepts name wherever it accepts id.
user_persona: A workflow-orchestrator or scheduled agent that re-runs its own setup script on every boot and needs that to be safe; a hook author retargeting an existing webhook/schedule to a new tool without losing its URL or quota slot.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given no trigger named webhook:ingest, When host.trigger.set(kind: webhook, tool: ingest) runs twice, Then the second call returns created: false, changed: [], host.trigger.list shows one row, and the quota counter is 1.

Given an existing webhook trigger, When set runs with the same name and a different tool, Then changed == ["tool_name"], the id and hook URL are unchanged, and a POST to the hook URL runs the new tool.
Given a schedule trigger, When set runs with the same name and a new cron, Then next_unix reflects the new cron and changed includes schedule.
Given a webhook named x, When set(kind: schedule, name: "x") runs, Then the error class is trigger_kind_mismatch and nothing changes.
Given a trigger, When host.trigger.remove(name: ...), pause(name), fire(name), and test(name) run, Then each behaves identically to the id form.
Given a database with two same-kind triggers for one tool before migration, When the migration runs, Then both survive with names <kind>:<tool> and <kind>:<tool>-2 and list shows both.
Given the quickstart webhook-inbox recipe, When read, Then its set step shows name and states that repeating the call is safe.

scope: migrations/0059_trigger_names.sql + src/db.rs: triggers.name TEXT (nullable, backfilled), unique (tenant_id, name) index; TriggerRow.name; insert_trigger/update_trigger/get_trigger_by_name; backfill_trigger_names_sync (P0 requirement 1 / AC6's collision-suffixing backfill, run unconditionally every migrate() call).

src/triggers.rs: the host.trigger.set dispatcher resolves name (default <kind>:<tool>), looks it up, refuses trigger_kind_mismatch on a different-kind collision, and routes create vs. update to each kind's own set_* function; annotate_set_result wraps every kind's response in {created, changed}; resolve() is the shared id-or-name lookup host.trigger.get/pause/resume/remove/fire (this module) and hooks::test/replay (hooks.rs) all call.

src/triggers.rs (set_schedule) / src/hooks.rs (set_event_trigger) / src/webhooks.rs (set_webhook_trigger): each kind's create path is unchanged in shape (still validates, quota-checks, inserts with the resolved name); each gains an update path that diffs the new config against the existing row, writes only when something actually changed (config_hash/tool_name equality is a no-op, requirement 6 / AC1's own 'changed: []' case), and never touches next_unix unless the schedule-shaped part of the config changed. webhooks::set_webhook_trigger's update never regenerates hook_id or the secret (AC2).

src/handler.rs: host.trigger.set's description/schema document name and the idempotence rule; host.trigger.get/pause/resume/remove/fire/test/replay schemas add name as an id alternative and drop id from required.
src/kinds/aliases.rs: the webhook-inbox and schedules quickstart recipes' host.trigger.set step shows name and carries a note stating repeated calls are safe (P0 requirement 5 / AC7).
contracts/host-tools.v1.json: regenerated (mcphost contract dump) to match the schema changes above.
non_goals: Changing hook signing or verification -- PRD-mcphost-event-trigger-self-test's territory, untouched here.
Versioning trigger configs or rollback -- an update overwrites the previous config_json outright, no history kept.
Allowing a name to move between kinds (webhook -> schedule) -- refused with trigger_kind_mismatch (non-goal, AC4); the caller must remove and re-set under a new name.
host.trigger.list's name_prefix filter (P1 requirement 7) -- no AC exercises it, not built.
host.export / host.registry_publish referencing triggers by name (P2 requirement 8) -- no AC exercises it, not built.

AC8 (the live/prod fleet-board retarget against tenant joe-test) -- deferred, operator-provisioned: it needs a real deployed box and an operator-held tenant env file this build agent never provisions or touches.

additional.open_question_default_taken: Open question default taken (PRD's own 'Drafted' answer): set without name on a tenant that already has two same-kind triggers for a tool is unreachable in practice since the default name <kind>:<tool> always resolves to exactly one of them (the first inserted, pre-AC6-migration) -- no separate trigger_name_ambiguous path was needed or built; the two triggers simply have distinct names (<kind>:<tool> and <kind>:<tool>-2) after migration 0059, and a bare set(tool, kind) with no name always targets the first.

five_whys_trace.q: Why give triggers a name instead of just making host.trigger.set compare the full (tool, kind, config) tuple and update on an exact config_hash match?
five_whys_trace.a: The whole point of 'set it again with a different tool/schedule/verify' is that the config is NOT identical to before -- a config_hash match can only ever catch the literal no-op case (already migration 0015's existing UNIQUE constraint), never the retarget case the 2026-09-30 incident actually hit. Only a caller-stable identity separate from the mutable config (a name) can answer 'is this the same logical trigger, just reconfigured?'.

five_whys_trace.q: Why default the name to <kind>:<tool_name> instead of requiring every caller to pass one explicitly?
five_whys_trace.a: Goal 1 is that re-running an existing setup script (written before this PRD, calling set with no name argument) becomes idempotent for free -- AC1's own wording is host.trigger.set(kind: webhook, tool: ingest) with no name at all. A mandatory name would be a breaking change to every existing caller; a default makes the common one-trigger-per-tool-per-kind case idempotent automatically while an explicit distinct name remains how a caller opts into a genuine second trigger (non-goal list / goal 4).

five_whys_trace.q: Why does an update never regenerate a webhook's secret or hook_id, even when other fields (tool, verify) change?
five_whys_trace.a: AC2 requires 'the id and hook URL are unchanged' after a tool retarget, and AC1 requires that an unchanged config_hash make 'changed: []' with no write -- a webhook's CREATE path mints a fresh random secret every call, so if UPDATE also regenerated it, the second of two identical set calls would never be a true no-op (the secret would always differ), breaking AC1 for the webhook kind specifically. Treating hook_id and the secret as immutable after creation is what keeps both AC1's idempotence and AC2's URL-stability true simultaneously.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does an update only recompute next_unix when the schedule-shaped part of the config (schedule/args/tz) actually changed, not on every update?
five_whys_trace.a: AC2's webhook case and a schedule update that only retargets tool share the same shape: a field having nothing to do with timing shouldn't silently shift when the trigger next fires. Recomputing next_unix unconditionally on any update (e.g. a tool-only retarget) would move a schedule that was already correctly due soon, which no AC asks for and would surprise an agent that only meant to change which tool runs.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the migration backfill run unconditionally every migrate() call (like migration 0049) instead of once, gated behind the same column-presence check that adds the name column itself?
five_whys_trace.a: Gating the Rust-side backfill on the ALTER TABLE's own one-time presence check would miss any row inserted between the ALTER TABLE and the backfill during a rolling deploy (a server process still running old code, mid-restart, could insert a NULL-name row after a newer process's migrate() already ran its one-time gate). An unconditional, idempotent-by-its-own-WHERE-clause backfill (AC6's own test re-runs migrate() twice and expects the second call to be a no-op) closes that window the same way migration 0049's own data-only backfill already does.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should set without name on a tenant that already has two same-kind triggers for that tool update the first or refuse as ambiguous? (PRD's own open question, drafted default: refuse trigger_name_ambiguous listing both names.)
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No separate ambiguity path was needed: after migration 0059's backfill, the two pre-existing duplicates have distinct names (<kind>:<tool> and <kind>:<tool>-2), so a bare set(tool, kind) with no name argument always resolves its default name to exactly the first one -- there is no state in which two triggers share one name for this lookup to be ambiguous over, since (tenant_id, name) is the unique index itself.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does the webhook kind's existing 'name' argument (previously required, alnum/underscore only, used as the inbox_<name> state table suffix) become a second, separate argument alongside the new trigger-identity name, or the same one?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: The same one: the PRD's own AC1 wording (host.trigger.set(kind: webhook, tool: ingest) with no name at all) requires the webhook kind's name argument to become optional too, and there is only one name key in the argument shape for a caller to pass. The inbox table is now named from the resolved trigger identity (inbox_<name>, including a default like webhook:ingest) rather than a second, separately-validated field; the previous alnum-only format restriction was dropped since tenant_state_tables.table_name is an ordinary parameterized string column, not a literal SQL identifier, so a colon in a default name is structurally safe.
